samples.summary: Removing the unconditional `clearCopyBuffer()` leaves a pending cut armed after a non-matching (external) paste
samples.evidence: `Sheet.paste` only discards the buffer inside the internal branch (`sheet.ts:2286`, guarded by `text === this.copyBuffer.text` and `isCut`). With the view's `clearCopyBuffer()` removed in both `view/worksheet.ts:4947` and `view/spreadsheet.ts:728`, a sequence of cut → paste of *different* clipboard content (text mismatch → external branch) leaves `copyBuffer.isCut === true` and `getCopyRange()` non-undefined, so the marching-ants overlay (`view/worksheet.ts:5600`) keeps advertising a pending cut and a later paste of the original text will still delete the source range, long after the user considers the gesture spent. The only reset left is the Escape handler at `view/worksheet.ts:5117`; `view/spreadsheet.ts` now contains no reference to `clearCopyBuffer` at all (grep for `clearCopyBuffer|copyRange|Escape` in that file returns nothing), so that view depends entirely on the embedded Worksheet's key handler to clear it.

samples.summary: `selectPastedRange` under-selects when the paste carried merged blocks
samples.evidence: `selectPastedRange(grid)` computes the selection from the pasted grid's bounding box via `rangeOf(grid)`. The change's own reasoning (`planPasteMerges`, sheet.ts:2390-2393) states that a merged block's covered cells hold nothing and are therefore absent from the grid, so the grid's box is strictly smaller than the region the paste actually wrote/merged. Example: copying `A1:C1` where `B1:C1` is merged yields a grid of `{A1,B1}`; pasted at row 3 the selection becomes `A3:B3` while the affected region is `A3:C3`, i.e. the selection clips the freshly created `B3:C3` block. The destination range is already computed correctly in `planPasteMerges` but is not passed to `selectPastedRange`.

samples.summary: `rangeOf` returns an inverted Infinity range for an empty grid with no guard
samples.evidence: For `grid.size === 0` the fold leaves `minR/minC = Infinity` and `maxR/maxC = -Infinity`, returning `[{r:Infinity,c:Infinity},{r:-Infinity,c:-Infinity}]` — an inverted, non-finite Range. The sole caller guards with `if (grid.size === 0) return;` (sheet.ts:2613), but the function is exported and now advertised as the shared bounding-box helper (the task doc asks other code to reuse it), so any future caller silently receives a poison Range instead of `undefined`. Behaviour matches the old `Math.min(...[])` result, so this is a carried-over gap, not a regression.

samples.summary: The new "a merged block may not straddle a freeze boundary" invariant is not enforced on `setFreezePane`, so a straddling block can still exist — and then becomes unmovable
samples.evidence: `planPasteMerges` (sheet.ts:2429) and `moveRangeTo` (sheet.ts:2685) now refuse operations that would produce a block crossing the freeze line, on the stated ground that the renderer cannot draw one. But `setFreezePane(frozenRows, frozenCols)` at sheet.ts:514 writes the freeze state with no check against `this.merges`, so freezing row 2 while `A1:A5` is merged creates exactly the state the new guards call undrawable. Worse, once such a block exists, `crossesFreezePane` is evaluated on the *translated* destination range only, so every drag-move that keeps it straddling is refused with `merge-move-frozen` — the block cannot be moved out of the bad state via drag. Searched: all references to `frozenRows|frozenCols` in sheet.ts, `canMergeSelection`, `setFreezePane`, `loadFreezePane`, and `crossesFreezePane` call sites; no merge validation exists on the freeze path.

samples.summary: External (TSV/HTML) paste still writes values into cells covered by a destination merge, which resurface as stale data on unmerge
samples.evidence: Only the internal branch computes `pastedMerges`/`replacedMerges`; the HTML (`html2grid(html, destStart)`, sheet.ts:2290) and TSV (`string2grid(destStart, text)`, sheet.ts:2294) branches leave both arrays empty, so `applyPasteMerges` early-returns and `setGrid` writes straight into cells covered by existing destination blocks. Normalizing only the *start* ref to the anchor fixes the first cell of the paste; every subsequent cell of a multi-cell external paste that lands under a block is still written hidden and reappears on unmerge — the same class of bug the change fixes for internal pastes. This is an explicitly documented non-goal (docs/tasks/active/20260912-sheets-paste-merge-propagation-todo.md:36-40) and pre-existing behaviour, recorded here only for completeness.
